Covered by 230+ unit and component tests plus Playwright end-to-end tests on desktop and mobile.

- [LinguaLine](https://github.com/Tridrik-Dey/LinguaLine): Chrome extension that overlays Italian subtitles with a live English translation underneath on YouTube and Netflix — built because I was learning Italian myself.

## About

I’m a Software Developer at BARS in Rome, a DocuSign partner. My day-to-day work is integrating DocuSign with enterprise systems — SAP, SharePoint, Microsoft Entra ID and HR platforms — using Java/Spring Boot, Node.js and TypeScript: backend APIs, OAuth 2.0 and SOAP/REST integrations, XML/JSON data contracts and the frontends around them.

Alongside my professional work I build AI projects independently: LLM applications, RAG architectures and AI agents. NVIDIA’s “Building RAG Agents with LLMs” course and the J.P. Morgan Software Engineering program sharpened how I think about scalable systems and AI-assisted development.

Before that I was a researcher at Università Roma Tre, designing and evaluating VR training systems with haptic feedback for Industry 4.0 and workplace safety. My path runs from electronics engineering through QA, operations and research to software development — so I care about systems that work for the people using them.

## DocuSign integration work (BARS, client names withheld)

Client names are hidden intentionally: this is my ongoing work at BARS, a DocuSign partner. The code stays private; here I describe the problem, my role, the architecture and the key decisions.

### SAP document data for DocuSign Maestro
Enterprise client · ongoing · Working prototype · ongoing

- Need: Before a document is signed, a Maestro workflow must pull the right document data from SAP — but users only know an internal request (RDA) number.
- Role: Built a private DocuSign Data IO Extension App in Node.js/Express that Maestro calls server-to-server. It queries SAP over SOAP and returns the document ID, title and status to the workflow.
- Flow: Maestro web form → Data IO extension (OAuth 2.0) → SAP (SOAP) → document data → signature step
- Key decision: OAuth 2.0 client credentials keep the extension a pure server-to-server service with no user login; a tunnel made the full SAP round-trip testable during development.
- Stack: DocuSign Maestro, Data IO Extension, Node.js, Express, OAuth 2.0, SOAP, SAP

### SharePoint purchase orders → DocuSign
Enterprise client · proof of concept · Proof of concept

- Need: Vendors must sign a purchase order together with every supporting document stored in SharePoint, sent as a single envelope.
- Role: Built a Java/Spring Boot service: from a PO number and revision it finds the SharePoint folder via Microsoft Graph, collects the PDFs, assembles the DocuSign envelope (main PO first) and sends it, returning envelope ID, status and warnings.
- Flow: PO request (REST) → Spring Boot → Microsoft Graph / SharePoint → envelope assembly → DocuSign → vendor
- Key decision: A mock mode runs the whole flow without Microsoft or DocuSign credentials, and the REST contract is designed for SAP to call later — so it can be demonstrated and tested before access to client systems exists.
- Stack: Java, Spring Boot, Microsoft Graph, SharePoint, DocuSign eSignature API, REST, Docker

### Signer data from Microsoft Entra ID
Enterprise client · proof of concept · Proof of concept

- Need: Signed documents must carry company and HR attributes of the sender and the employee, ready for archiving in a document-management system.
- Role: Built a TypeScript service that resolves envelope roles, matches users by email in Microsoft Entra ID via Microsoft Graph, and writes the mapped attributes as envelope custom fields.
- Flow: DocuSign envelope → roles → email → Microsoft Graph /users → mapped attributes → envelope custom fields
- Key decision: Which roles and attributes are used lives in a mapping file, so the business can change it without a code change.
- Stack: TypeScript, Node.js, Microsoft Graph, Entra ID, DocuSign eSignature API, Vitest

### HR e-signature and archiving to Zucchetti
Italian enterprise client · ongoing · Analysis + phase-1 prototype · ongoing

- Need: HR onboarding documents should be signed in person on a tablet and then filed automatically in each employee’s folder in Zucchetti HR.
- Role: Wrote the bilingual functional analysis (EN/IT) and built the phase-1 prototype: in-person signing, archiving and an action log, on mock data.
- Flow: HR on tablet → in-person signature → signed documents → Zucchetti HR (employee folder) → action log
- Key decision: DocuSign and Zucchetti sit behind adapters, so the real integrations replace the mocks without changing the UI or the business rules.
- Stack: DocuSign, Zucchetti HR, Node.js, Adapters, Functional analysis

## Research

At Università Roma Tre I worked on how people learn safety-critical tasks when they can feel what they’re doing — not just see it.

- Designed VR training systems that add haptic (touch) feedback to industrial procedures.
- Evaluated how these systems support training for Industry 4.0 environments and workplace safety.
- Brought the research mindset — hypotheses, measurement, iteration — into how I build software today.

**What kind of role are you looking for?** Software developer roles where Java/Spring Boot backends meet integrations — DocuSign, SAP, Microsoft 365 — and, ideally, AI and RAG.
